problem: End-to-end RL ObjectNav policies acting on raw egocentric observations struggle; the Habitat Challenge 2021 ObjectNav task needs methods that exploit semantics and mapping and decouple planning from low-level control.
motivation: ObjectNav requires reaching an instance of a target class without prior knowledge of the environment. The authors explore sensor fusion, semantic segmentation and a top-down semantic map, with a learned global planner separated from a local planner so each can be swapped.
key_idea: Build an online top-down semantic map from Yolact++ segmentation, depth, GPS and compass, and train a PPO global policy (BEyond) to predict a goal coordinate (Cartesian or polar) that a pre-trained DD-PPO local planner follows.
insight: The paper offers little analysis. The decoupled design and imitation-augmented reward are presented as its main aspects, but no ablation supports them. The 0.00 SR/SPL results, despite ranking fourth, show that the method essentially fails to reach goals, and that the ranking reflects weak competition rather than strong performance.
method: Semantic segmentation: Yolact++ fine-tuned to the 21 Habitat 2021 ObjectNav classes (subset of MP3D's 40), confidence threshold 0.55.

Semantic map: predictions projected with depth, GPS and compass into a 512x512 top-view map (0.05 m cells) with 25 channels (obstacles, 21 classes, occupancy max-pool, visited trajectory, current position), center-cropped to 25x256x256.

BEyond global policy: Actor-Critic taking the map, target class ID and orientation; trained with PPO for ~1M steps on Habitat; outputs two continuous coordinates sampled from a Gaussian and squashed by a sigmoid.
Cartesian variant: output is scaled to map cells as a global goal; A* over the occupancy channel gives a local goal, converted to polar and passed to the local planner.
Polar variant: outputs distance rho and orientation phi (mapped to [-pi, pi]) as the global goal, fed to the same local planner.
Local planner: DD-PPO actor-critic taking RGB-D and the local goal, outputting STOP/MOVE_FORWARD/TURN_LEFT/TURN_RIGHT.
Reward: step penalty -1e-4, +1e-3 if the action matches a greedy oracle (imitation term), a distance-to-goal progress term, and +2.5 on success.

setting.backbone: Yolact++ (fine-tuned) + BEyond actor-critic (PPO, trained from scratch) + DD-PPO local planner (pre-trained)
setting.training_data: Yolact++ fine-tuned on Matterport3D 21 classes; BEyond trained ~1M steps with PPO in Habitat
setting.action_space: global goal coordinates (continuous) converted to low-level discrete STOP/FORWARD/TURN_LEFT/TURN_RIGHT via local planner
setting.privileged: greedy oracle with perfect scene knowledge used for the reward during training only; none at test

results: The method ranked 4th on both the Minival and Test-Standard leaderboards, but with SPL and success rate of 0.00. Its SoftSPL was 0.14 (Minival) and 0.08 (Test), well below the winner TreasureHunt (SR 0.27 and 0.21). It only matched or slightly beat the DD-PPO baseline in distance to goal.
limitations: Success rate and SPL are 0.00, so the agent never successfully completes an episode; no ablations or analysis are given.
Very short training (~1M steps) and reliance on a two-stage pipeline with a frozen local planner.
Different variants were submitted to different phases, preventing a clean comparison.
